Removing the sole link can therefore leave the issue filtered until the cooldown expires, up to six hours. Assignment has no direct invalidation; it only affects the quiet-TTL branch. Store a PR metadata or linkage fingerprint with the head SHA, and invalidate the record when that value changes. This is a narrow metadata edge case, but it can delay redispatch after a maintainer detaches the checkpoint PR.

Linux limits a single argument to 128 KiB (`MAX_ARG_STRLEN`). A timeline array contains full `commented` events with actor objects and comment bodies. A blocked issue with many coordination comments can exceed that limit. `jq` then fails to start. The `2>/dev/null` on Line 102 hides the error. The caller sees a non-4 status and runs `return 1`. +# draft projected status:blocked. The dispatch candidate filter skips
+# status:blocked and the stale-blocked sweep resolves only dependency blocks,
+# so those drafts were never continued, merged or surfaced. Runners on older
+# versions keep producing that state until they update.

+# nothing else; any unreadable or ambiguous read means no write:
+#   - an open issue whose only status label is status:blocked, without a
+#     protective label;
+#   - exactly one open origin:worker draft PR closing it;
+#   - the newest trusted CLAIM_RELEASED carries a continuable, non-terminal
+#     reason, and no claim or live lease follows it;
+#   - the newest `labeled status:blocked` event is that runner's, inside the
+#     release projection window;
+#   - assignees are only that runner;
+#   - no audit marker exists for that release and the per-PR cap is unmet.

+# Sourced by pulse-merge.sh. Reuses pulse-merge-partial-continuation.sh

+		| select(names | any(. == "hold-for-review" or . == "no-auto-dispatch"

**Skip identifier-less events after validating timestamps.** A normal worker run can use an `issue-N` session key without `WORKER_ISSUE_NUMBER`. The terminal blocker branch then runs, but its logger call omits issue and repository arguments. The resulting `issue_number: null` event is read by the breaker from the same log. The current jq filter treats it as malformed, aborts the window, and fails open. This can prevent three valid distinct events from tripping the breaker.
